item.title: His father's death nearly ended his boxing career. Now he's rebuilding it beneath Sixth and Market
item.description: Professional boxers Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic, left, and Lawrence King spar at Abaddon Fight Club Gym in San Francisco. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) In the summer of 2025, Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic was ready to quit boxing. Widely regarded as the best fighter to come out of San Francisco in a generation, the light heavyweight was a nine-time national amateur boxing champion, with more than 100 fights to his name. He was 9-1 since turning pro. At 27, he was in his prime. But in August of that year, his desire to keep fighting disappeared when his father, Sheldon Callum, overdosed on fentanyl at the Western Hotel on Leavenworth Street in the Tenderloin . Callum died just a few blocks from the Turk Street apartment building where the family lived when Mahmutovic was a kid. In losing Callum, Mahmutovic lost not just his dad, but the man who had coached him since he started fighting competitively at age 8. That's nearly two decades of predawn workouts and late-night drives, convention centers and casinos, drafty high school gyms and damp basement fight clubs. The road had taken them from the Tenderloin to Reno, Kansas City to Albuquerque, Tijuana to Ukraine. Professional boxer Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic rests after a 12-round sparring session. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) Boxing is a hard business, and with his dad gone Mahmutovic wasn't sure he had the heart to keep going. He had a wife and two young sons to take care of. He had a full-time job installing and testing fire alarm systems. It wasn't like he was getting rich in the boxing ring. He had rent to pay in Oakland. Meanwhile at Abaddon Fight Club, a bare-bones basement boxing gym at Sixth and Market streets in San Francisco, Jason "JP" Peterson wondered about Mahmutovic. Peterson had opened the gym in 2023, and in the months before Callum died, Mahmutovic had started stopping by the gym to work out or spar. Now Mahmutovic was nowhere to be found. "All of a sudden he disappeared," Peterson said. "He deleted everything off his social media. I was like, ‘Bro, what are you doing?' He was kind of like, ‘Look, man, it's not the same anymore.' His exact words were, ‘I don't know if I want to do this anymore.'" Suray "Sugar" Mahmutovic has his gloves tied by coach Jason Peterson before sparring at Abaddon Fight Club. (Santiago Mejia/S.F. Chronicle) A former pro boxer and Hells Angels member with a lengthy criminal record, Peterson could relate to what the boxer was going through. He had lost his father to COVID while serving a 10-year federal prison sentence for distribution of methamphetamine. item.title: Arsenal stars given FPL ban after team news leak
item.description: Arsenal stars given FPL ban after team news leak Arsenal players, like many professional footballers and supporters, enjoy participating in the popular Fantasy Premier League (FPL) game. However, the game has reportedly become an unexpected source of team news, prompting Mikel Arteta to introduce restrictions on how his players use it. The Gunners do not deliberately reveal their starting line ups, but selecting themselves in their FPL teams can provide supporters and opposing clubs with clues about their availability and potential involvement in upcoming matches. This became an issue ahead of Arsenal’s game against Liverpool at Anfield . Christos Tzolis had only returned to training a few days before the encounter, and there was considerable uncertainty over whether he would be fit enough to start. However, the Greek star selected himself in his FPL team and even made himself captain, suggesting that he expected to feature from the beginning. This reportedly did not go down well with Arteta, who wants to keep his selection decisions private until matchday. Arteta introduces FPL restrictions According to the Daily Mail , Arteta has now banned his players from selecting themselves in their respective FPL teams. The restriction also means Arsenal players are no longer allowed to include their teammates in their fantasy squads. The reported decision is intended to prevent accidental leaks of team information through the popular fantasy football competition. Even without deliberately sharing confidential information, players could provide useful clues about the manager’s selection plans through their choices. For a club competing at the highest level, keeping opponents guessing about the starting line up can be an important part of match preparation. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Tzolis makes changes to his fantasy team The report also reveals that Tzolis removed all Arsenal players from his FPL team ahead of the Gunners’ next fixture . That change appears to reflect the new restriction introduced by Arteta and suggests that the players have been made aware of the manager’s expectations. Although fantasy football is generally regarded as harmless entertainment, the situation demonstrates how even small details can attract attention when professional footballers participate in public competitions. Arsenal will now want their players to avoid providing unnecessary clues about team selection, whether intentionally or otherwise. item.title: 49ers will face an ‘elite defense' Sunday. Can the team withstand Vikings' rush?
item.description: Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan will look for ways to make a dent in a Minnesota Vikings defense that leads the NFL with 37 sacks when the teams meet Sunday night in Mexico City. (John Froschauer/Associated Press) The last time Brock Purdy played a Brian Flores-led defense, he was in awe. On Sept. 15, 2024, right after losing 23-17 to the Minnesota Vikings , the San Francisco 49ers quarterback approached their defensive coordinator at midfield. "Your scheme is crazy!" Purdy told Flores, as picked up by surrounding microphones, after he was sacked a season-high six times and blitzed on 52% (23 of 44) of his dropbacks. Purdy still threw for 319 yards that afternoon, but he never looked settled. The 49ers went 3-for-13 on third and fourth down. They put together only one scoring drive before the fourth quarter. And yet, if Purdy thought Flores designed an aggressive scheme back in 2024, the tape Purdy has been watching ahead of the 49ers' Week 11 game against the Vikings in Mexico City must look extraterrestrial. Minnesota, which blitzed on a league-high 39.9% of dropbacks two seasons ago, has blitzed on a league-high 69.3% of dropbacks this season. That's nearly 30% higher than the next-most blitz happy team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Vikings' pressure rate (49.8%) and sack rate (12%) also comfortably lead the NFL. Flores does it with a sense of chaotic unpredictability, too: Five Vikings have recorded at least three sacks this season. "He's more unique than all the other 31 guys. He's the one guy who commits to this, and it's not just a fad for these nine games or whatever," 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said of Flores. "A lot of times when you go into an NFL game, the pressure is really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are (the plays) where everything can come. When you play against Brian, it's 70 straight plays of that." "They're going to throw a lot at you, right?" Niners offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak added. "They're playing in this scheme where they're throwing different blitzes at you, different coverages, but the way they're tied together and the way that they can all play so fast and decisively, that's what makes this an elite defense to me. I think if you tried to go and install this defense in a new place, it would take a while to get a group of guys to play the way they play. They're violent." item.title: “Why is This Even An Idea?” – Yankees Fans React As NY Re-Signs 32 y/o Pitcher With Long Injury History To 2-Year Deal
item.description: Jonathan Loáisiga - NY Yankees | © Instagram /@loaisiga_43 Jonathan Loáisiga is headed back to the Bronx after agreeing to a two-year, $18 million deal with the Yankees, with a 2029 club option, according to ESPN’s Jorge Castillo . The Nicaraguan spent eight years with New York before the team declined his club option last offseason, making him a free agent. Loáisiga later signed a minor league contract with the Diamondbacks and earned a spot on the 2026 opening-day roster after an impressive spring training. When news of the 32-year-old’s reported return to New York broke on social media, fans shared their reactions. Loáisiga has had an injury-ridden history in the MLB, starting with a shoulder injury in 2019. The injury resurfaced in 2022 and 2023, followed by elbow injuries from 2023 to 2025. He also had a back injury in 2025, and missed a large chunk of the 2024 season with a torn UCL. “Like why is this even an idea lol,” one fan commented. Loáisiga appeared in a career-high 67 games for the Diamondbacks last season, finishing with a 7-3 record, a 2.42 ERA, 48 strikeouts, and a 1.03 WHIP over 67 innings. It was a clear resurgence for the injury-prone reliever, who last posted a sub-3 ERA in 2021 with the Yankees, going 9-4 in 57 appearances. Loáisiga has made only 11 starts in his big-league career, but his work as a reliever has been eye-catching. Still, his multiple IL stints over the years will be a concern for the Bronx Bombers. The Yankees Continue Reshaping Their Bullpen This Offseason The Yankees parted ways with two pitchers Friday, declining to tender contracts to Fernando Cruz and Luis Gil . Both were projected to earn $2.3 million through arbitration. New York tendered contracts to its other seven arbitration-eligible players: José Caballero, Luis García Jr., Clarke Schmidt, Anthony Volpe, Ryan Weathers, Heliot Ramos, and Austin Wells. As the franchise continues to reshape its bullpen, new addition Loáisiga is set to join fellow relievers David Bednar , who agreed to a one-year, $23.15 million contract, and Tim Hill, as well as free agent Paul Blackburn, who has also been strongly linked to a return to the Bronx. item.title: Australia's Chaudhary downs England in tetchy first T20
item.description: Nikhil Chaudhary was playing his fourth T20 for Australia [Getty Images] First T20, Melbourne Cricket Ground England 187-9 (20 overs): Brook 65 (28), Banton 39 (22); Chaudhary 2-21 Australia 191-7 (19.5 overs): Chaudhary 66 (38) Australia won by three wickets Scorecard Unlikely Australia international Nikhil Chaudhary rattled England and was the match-winner in a tense and tetchy final-over victory in the first T20 international in Melbourne. Born in Delhi and a team-mate of India captain Shubman Gill in Indian domestic cricket, Chaudhary only switched to representing Australia after the Covid pandemic meant he got stuck in Brisbane celebrating his 24th birthday. Progression through Australian club and domestic cricket followed - plus a stint working in a Mexican restaurant - before the 30-year-old played his standout performance to date in his fourth international at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Helping restrict England to 187-9 despite Harry Brook's fireworks in smashing 65 off 28 balls, Chaudhary took 2-21 with his mystery spin and then hit 66 to steer Australia within 20 runs of victory. The elegant right-hander appeared to anger both Liam Dawson and Sam Curran during his knock and the MCG crowd loudly booed England as the tourists slowed the game in the final moments. "You always know it is going to be a big game against England so there is going to be some chirp," said Chaudhary. Curran was left with 11 to defend from the last over but all-rounder Jack Edwards finished with 25 not out as Australia completed their highest chase on home soil with three wickets and one ball remaining. The win offers some relief to Australia - an XI featuring a host of new faces putting aside the ongoing sandpaper scandal to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series. England can level the contest in Gold Coast on Tuesday. Lehmann again denies knowing about sandpaper plot Chaudhary lets cricket do the talking After all of the off-field issues that have overshadowed this tour, this was a welcome entertaining game of cricket. England lost Phil Salt to the first ball of the match and afterwards there was boundary-hitting, comically bad fielding by Australia, a bit of needle and a grandstand finish. Chaudhary should take the headlines. After opener Jake Fraser-McGurk fell in the first over and Mitchell Marsh was sluggish in making 37, he found scoring more straightforward. He repeatedly targeted the off side and, after Australia lost 3-13 from 143-3, he pressed on the accelerator by hitting Will Jacks for six and Jamie Overton for two fours. The incidents with Dawson and Curran appeared innocuous but words were exchanged. The umpire intervened in the Curran spat to encourage Chaudhary to continue his innings. By hitting Overton to deep square-leg at the end of the 18th over, he allowed England back into the game. item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 14: Head Coach Will Wade of the LSU Tigers in action against the UCF Knights held at Pete Maravich Assembly Center on October 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, LA. (Photo by Kristen Young/LSU/University Images via Getty Images} The funny thing about Will Wade is that nearly everyone understands he is, at heart, a grifter. NC State fans knew it when they pressured A.D. Boo Corrigan to hire him. It should not have surprised anyone that he used the Wolfpack as a quick way station before bolting back to LSU at the first opportunity. LSU fans know this too. They simply love a rogue, which is why they embraced the return of the Harold Hill of college basketball. Since landing back in Baton Rouge, Wade has done exactly what anyone paying attention expected: he has pushed the envelope on eligibility. He recruited multiple players with serious questions about their status, including some who had already signed professional contracts and spent time with NBA teams. Fellow rogue Lane Kiffin had already tried something similar on the football side with players who had NFL experience. Together, the two efforts thoroughly outraged the rest of the SEC. Memorably, conference members went so far as to float the idea of expelling the Tigers altogether. (Interesting intellectual exercise: who would take them if it came to that? The Big Ten? Hard to see. The Big 12? Maybe, maybe not. The ACC? Seems pretty unlikely.) The pot nearly boiled over during Kiffin’s hijinks. Now, with Wade’s RJ Luis mess, things have heated back up again. Luis received favorable rulings from two Louisiana judges—Ronald R. Johnson and Will Jorden—both of whom are elected rather than appointed. Jorden’s order effectively blocked the SEC from punishing LSU for rostering Luis. After a conversation with SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, however, LSU President Wade Rousse, following “further review,” instructed Wade that Luis could no longer play. Rousse was no doubt made aware of other SEC schools weighing retaliatory measures—boycotting LSU games or revisiting the nuclear option of simply expelling the Tigers from the Situational Ethics Conference. After all of that, Luis announced he would “stand down” from the team. His lawyer, Tony Clayton, has threatened unspecified civil actions. Clayton is not just a private attorney in this matter. He is the District Attorney for Louisiana’s 18th Judicial District, which covers West Baton Rouge Parish. LSU sits just across the river in the 19th Judicial District, where Hillar Moore is the District Attorney. Both attorneys and both judges graduated from Southern University Law Center in Baton Rouge. Clayton and Moore overlapped there (Moore in 1989, Clayton in 1991). Jorden previously worked under Moore as a prosecutor, and Moore now prosecutes cases in front of Jorden. item.description: Preview | Lazio-Juventus Women The Women’s First Team return to Serie A Women action with a Matchday 8 game against Lazio in Rome. Having beaten OH Leuven and secured a place in the next round of the UEFA Women’s Champions League in midweek, the Bianconere now want to build on their improving league form. Let’s get up to speed ahead of the game with some pre-match stats. INTERESTING FACTS Juventus are one of four teams to have scored at least five goals against Lazio in a Serie A match (alongside Fiorentina, Inter and Milan), but they are the only ones to have done so on two occasions: a 5-0 home win on 13 November 2021 and a 5-1 away win on 24 April 2022. Juventus have won their last three Serie A matches and have not managed four consecutive wins since the period between November 2024 and January 2025. Juventus are the team with the most sequences of at least 10 passes in this Serie A season, both in total (105, at least 40 more than any other side in the competition) and in terms of those that have led to a shot or a touch in the opposition’s penalty area (18). Alba Redondo has been directly involved in at least one goal in all seven Serie A matches she has played so far (6 goals + 3 assists); since Opta began recording key passes (2020/21), only one player has reached eight: Tabitha Chawinga with Inter between December 2022 and March 2023 – Manuela Giugliano could also equal the record this matchday, having been involved in at least one goal in each of the first seven matchdays. item.title: ‘You just can’t’: Steve Kerr says there’s something Yaxel Lendeborg must stop doing right now
item.description: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images Yaxel Lendeborg has been in the headlines for one reason or another since joining the Golden State Warriors. First, it was his altercation with Luka Doncic on the court that caught everyone’s attention. Then, his incredible run of form made him a fan favourite. Now, Lendeborg and the Warriors are struggling, and that poor run seems to be affecting the rookie a lot more than it should. Coach Steve Kerr has claimed that Lendeborg needs to stop. Steve Kerr tells Yaxel Lendeborg to stop being ‘too emotional’ Lendeborg wears his heart on his sleeve, and that is a good trait to have. That brought the best out of the 24-year-old early on in the season, but he has struggled in recent games, much like his teammates. Lendeborg has been affected so much that he decided to cut his hair and has looked beyond dejected on the bench in more than one game. Kerr has noticed that, and he has urged his rookie to stop being too emotional. He said on 95.7 The Game: “He is (down on himself). I think it’s actually been discussed publicly. He hung the towel over his head on the road trip somewhere, I can’t remember what game it was, maybe New Orleans. “Draymond actually talked to him about that, to keep an even keel. He wants to be great, and he cares so much, so he’s being a little bit too emotional with the ups and the downs. “You just can’t operate that way. The season will grind you to death if you do. “I love his investment and how much he wants to play and wants to win, but it has got to be more of a day-to-day stable approach, get better, understand how long the season is, and we’re all going to be better off if we keep an even keel.” Yaxel Lendeborg is not the problem for the Golden State Warriors Lendeborg will be the first one to admit that he hasn’t been great for the Warriors lately, but the real problem is their over-reliance on Steph Curry. When the 38-year-old superstar is in the team, the Warriors come out on top more often than not and play like they are one of the contenders. In his absence, however, it has been a different story. The Warriors desperately need Curry back in the side, but the fact that they are so reliant on a 38-year-old is a big problem. Mike Dunleavy Jr. has to find a way to fix that, but whether he can in the middle of the season is an entirely different story. It remains to be seen what will happen to the Warriors, but until Curry comes back, we just can’t see how they will look as good again. item.description: Sam Leavitt and Lane Kiffin. © Imagn Lane Kiffin’s first season with LSU has not met expectations. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban believes LSU is in this current situation because of quarterback Sam Leavitt’s mistakes. The Tigers are 6-4 overall and 3-4 in SEC this season. On The Pat McAfee Show Friday, Saban highlighted LSU’s problems and how Leavitt’s mistakes have played a role in the team’s current situation. “What’s LSU’s issue? Turning the ball over, and the quarterback’s been responsible for that to a large degree,” Saban said. “I’m not killing the guy. I respect him as a competitor. He plays hard. He makes a lot of plays. If you could just eliminate his bad plays, LSU would be in a completely different position than they’re in right now because they turn the ball over, what, six times in the last three or four games in the red zone and get no points out of it. I mean, that’s tough to overcome.” Saban questioned whether Leavitt has made any progress this season. Leavitt arrived in Baton Rouge with high expectations after an impressive 2024 season at Arizona State. He threw for 2,885 yards and 24 touchdowns while recording just six interceptions, alongside 443 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns. His performances helped Arizona State finish 11-3, win the Big 12 title, and earn the program’s first College Football Playoff appearance. Speaking on The Pat McAfee Show , he said: “And I would like to say to Daniel, I’ll never forget what he did during those first ten weeks last year. item.description: FILE PHOTO - Werder Bremen coach Daniel Thioune acknowledges the fans after the German Bundesliga soccer match between Werder Bremen and SC Paderborn 07 at the Weserstadion. (is associated with: «Werder Bremen extends contract with coach Daniel Thioune») Carmen Jaspersen/dpa Daniel Thioune has extended his coaching contract with Werder Bremen, the Bundesliga football club said on Saturday before the next day's Northern Derby against Hamburg. The club did not disclose the new duration of Thioune's contract. "We are completely convinced by Daniel's work. He achieved the set goal last season with great meticulousness despite a difficult situation, and has visibly stabilized and further developed the team this season," Werder's Managing Director of Football Clemens Fritz said in a statement. The 52-year-old coach's original contract was set to expire at the end of the current season. Fritz added: "He connects very well with the team thanks to his humane, clear and direct manner, is very focused on the substance of his work, and has managed to quickly mould the newly formed squad into a cohesive unit." Born in Georgsmarienhütte, Lower Saxony, Thioune took over at Werder on February 4 after the Bremen club parted ways with coach Horst Steffen. Thioune went on to guide the club to safety from relegation. "I am having a tremendous amount of fun being able to work with this team at Werder. We have great characters in this group, and we are succeeding more and more in playing our brand of football," he said. Alongside Thioune's contract, the agreements with assistant coaches Jan Hoepner and Christian Gross were also extended. Thioune previously worked at Fortuna Düsseldorf, Sunday's opponent Hamburg, and Osnabrück - the club for which he also made 170 appearances as a player. From his time in Osnabrück, he also knows current Hamburg coach Merlin Polzin, who served as his assistant at both Osnabrück and in Hamburg. The two moved together from Lower Saxony to Hamburg, where Polzin remained following Thioune's dismissal in May 2021. To this day, the two remain close friends. On Sunday, Thioune and Polzin will face off as opponents at Bremen's Weser Stadium.

By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years.
